articles.title: Three-week on-site audit at OpenAI reveals major gaps in AI safety monitoring
articles.content:
External auditors from METR and Redwood Research spent three weeks on-site at OpenAI examining the company's internal monitoring system for AI agents and found significant gaps, with up to 25 percent of agent traffic from models at the GPT-5.5 class and above going unmonitored. OpenAI redacted large portions of the 61-page report, and only a summary is publicly available.

articles.title: 男子醉酒后车机自动报警被判不构成自首：系统可以替你报警但不能替你自首
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，由于把“110”设成紧急联系人，浙江一男子醉驾后，车辆发现异常上报给车企紧急救援中心并自动报警，后续被民警当场查获。该男子显然不服，并辩称这属于自首。那么，这类车机触发的报警，法律上到底能不能认定为自首？据央视《法治在线》今日报道，这类新型醉驾案在法律上不能被认定为自首。车辆紧急救援系统自动拨出的报警电话，不能替驾驶人完成“自动投案”。此次事件发生于 2026 年 3 月 19 日晚，周某酒后驾驶一辆小型普通客车返回家中，途中开启车辆驾驶辅助功能，后因酒劲上头困意难忍而选择在路边停车，随后在驾驶位昏睡起来。但此时车辆仍处于启动状态，车企紧急救援中心监测到车辆长时间无人接管、多次呼叫驾驶人无应答后，按照应急处置流程拨打了周某预设的紧急联系人电话 ——110。民警到场后发现周某身上有明显酒气，经呼气检测及后续血样鉴定，其血液酒精含量为 186mg/100ml，远超 80mg/100ml 的醉驾标准。周某对醉驾事实供认不讳，但又提出车辆自动报警应视为委托投案，且本人始终留在现场未逃离，请求认定为自首。法院没有接受这一逻辑。浙江缙云县人民法院对该案作出判决，认定周某不构成自首，以危险驾驶罪判处拘役一个月，并处罚金 2000 元，一审宣判后周某未上诉，判决已生效。法院指出，根据刑法第六十七条，自首须同时具备自动投案与如实供述两个要件，而“自动投案”的核心在于行为人基于自己的意志，主动、自愿地将自己置于司法机关控制之下。承办法官从主观与客观两个层面拆解了周某的处境：主观上，周某因醉酒昏睡已丧失对车辆的实质管控，车企拨出电话的原因是车辆长时间无人接管、呼叫无回应，目的是排查驾驶人的人身安全风险，并非受周某委托代为投案，周某本人缺乏投案的意识；客观上，周某滞留现场是因为醉酒后无法继续驾车而被动形成的结果，并非主动留在现场等候公安机关处理。技术系统按预设程序执行的报警动作，与行为人自主作出的投案决定，在刑法评价上不能混为一谈。这一认定与最高人民法院此前明确的裁判规则相衔接。2026 年 2 月发布的指导性案例 271 号（王某群危险驾驶案）指出，车载辅助驾驶系统不能代替驾驶人成为驾驶主体，驾驶人激活辅助驾驶功能后仍是实际执行驾驶任务的人，负有确保行车安全的责任；即使驾驶人利用配件逃避系统监测、不在主驾驶位实际操控，仍应作为驾驶主体承担法律责任。同年 3 月，最高人民法院工作报告进一步写入“驾驶人醉酒后启用辅助驾驶功能仍应承担刑事责任”。在上述指导性案例中，王某群血液酒精含量为 114.5mg/100ml，因加装“智驾神器”坐到副驾驶位睡觉，最终被判处拘役一个月十五日、罚金 4000 元。与王某群案相比，周某案的特殊性在于争议焦点从“是否构成危险驾驶罪”前移到了“到案方式能否折抵量刑”—— 辅助驾驶没有免除驾驶人的刑事责任，车辆自动报警也没有替驾驶人创造自首情节。辅助驾驶与自动驾驶之间的责任分界，在这类案件中反复成为前提性问题。依据国家标准《汽车驾驶自动化分级》，L0 至 L2 级均属辅助驾驶，系统仅提供预警或短暂的横纵向控制，驾驶人必须全程监管并随时准备接管，是唯一的责任主体；L3 级有条件自动驾驶是责任主体从驾驶员向车企转移的节点，系统激活期间发生事故，责任指向生产企业。当前市面上绝大多数家用车型搭载的仍是 L2 级系统，这意味着“开启辅助驾驶后放任不管”本身即构成对法定义务的违反。民事层面遵循同一逻辑：因驾驶人分心、疏于接管或违规使用辅助驾驶导致事故，驾驶员承担主要乃至全部责任；只有当鉴定确认车辆存在产品缺陷或功能故障，且与事故存在直接因果关系时，车企才进入赔偿责任的范围。2026 年 10 月北京金融法院联合发布的智能网联汽车保险纠纷报告进一步提出了“对外顺位赔付、对内追偿归属”的双层结构，试图在受害人救济与驾驶人、车企之间的最终责任分配之间作出区分。相关阅读：《男子醉酒后开智驾在超车道停车睡着，被判拘役 1 个月处罚金 2000 元》《一男子醉酒后使用辅助驾驶发生事故并冲卡，被拘役三个月 + 罚款九千元》《奕境曾清林谈“武汉首例醉酒辅助驾驶司机被判刑”：事件本质是醉驾，不是智驾》

articles.title: 长城魏牌二代蓝山全球首秀定档 10 月 27 日，搭载 Hi-4 插电混动系统
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，长城汽车今日宣布魏牌二代蓝山全球首秀定档 10 月 27 日。新车采用方盒子设计，搭载由 2.0T 发动机组成的 Hi-4 插电混动系统。据介绍，魏牌二代蓝山主打“东方豪华”，尺寸为 5300×2050×1960mm、轴距 3010mm，轮胎规格 275/50 R21。新车搭载 2.0T 混动专用发动机，匹配 4 挡混动专用变速箱，电机功率为前 110kW、后 220kW，内置 66.6kWh（1/3C）电池。IT之家注意到，官方公布了该车的曜石黑、浅蓝外观配色，新车也已经在工信部完成申报。其尺寸为 5300×2050×1960mm、轴距 3010mm，轮胎规格 275/50 R21。新车正面配备直瀑式镀铬格栅，前大灯是复古风的圆形设计，尾部印有“蓝山”标识，采用平开式尾门，尾灯为双圆形组合，此次公布的影像中，新车用上了大饼轮毂，豪华气息又增加了不少。

articles.title: 国家邮政局召开邮政快递业安全治理规范化座谈会：要持续深入推进“反内卷”工作
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，据国家邮政局，10 月 22 日至 23 日，国家邮政局在河南洛阳召开邮政快递业安全治理规范化座谈会。会议要求，各级邮政管理部门要强化行业监管核心职能，大力加强行业安全监管，维护快递市场秩序。各企业要把安全责任牢牢扛在肩上，统筹发展和安全，进一步抓实抓细行业安全各项工作。会议强调，要聚焦突出问题和关键环节，以更大力度更实举措做好行业安全工作：一是大力整治生产安全突出隐患。要强化重大事故隐患排查整治，深入整治消防隐患，严格规范外包管理，持续完善企业安全管理体系。二是突出抓好寄递渠道风险防范。要抓好寄递安全“三项制度”落实，抓实抓细行业反诈工作，加强寄递物品安全管理，加强信息安全防范。三是强化事前事中事后全链条监管。要加强事前准入与事中事后管理衔接，抓好两项强制性国家标准执行，加强协议用户规范管理，提升广大群众用邮安全感。四是持续深入推进“反内卷”工作。要确保末端派费稳定，深化成本核算指导，严肃整治跨区揽件行为，企业总部要优化对所属服务网络的考核管理规则，不得层层加码、转嫁经营成本。五是加强风险研判，及时化解矛盾纠纷，全力做好行业稳定工作。IT之家注意到，国家邮政局于 10 月 19 日公布 2026 年 1-9 月邮政行业运行情况，整理主要内容如下：1—9 月，邮政行业业务收入（不包括邮政储蓄银行直接营业收入）累计完成 13893.1 亿元，同比增长 5.8%。其中，快递业务收入累计完成 11634.4 亿元，同比增长 7.2%。1—9 月，邮政行业寄递业务量累计完成 1641.3 亿件，同比增长 3.7%。其中，快递业务量累计完成 1513.0 亿件，同比增长 4.3%。

articles.title: OpenAI 联合研究机构部署数千个 AI 智能体：32 分钟分析数百万个小鼠脑细胞，相当于人类数月时间
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，OpenAI 联合 PerturbAI 和斯克里普斯研究所（Scripps Research），利用数千个 AI 智能体分析数百万个小鼠脑细胞的生物学数据，整个分析过程仅耗时 32 分钟。研究团队估计，如果由人类研究人员逐项分析实验结果并检索相关文献，完成同等工作可能需要数月到一年。根据 OpenAI 10 月 21 日发布的介绍，这项研究使用了专为生命科学研究设计的 GPT-Rosalind 模型，分析一份覆盖整个小鼠大脑的 CRISPR 图谱。该图谱记录了不同基因受到干预后，各类脑细胞产生的变化，有助于研究人员了解基因功能及其与疾病之间的潜在联系。研究团队采用分布式 AI 智能体架构，将大量分析任务拆分后并行执行。每个智能体负责研究一种基因干预，分析相关细胞的反应，并检索科学文献，为观察到的变化寻找可能的生物学解释。随后，研究人员将各智能体的报告整合为一份名为“Reasoning Atlas”的推理图谱，关联基因、细胞变化、参考文献和潜在作用机制。研究人员发现，分布式智能体不仅能够复现已有研究中的部分结论，还提出了一些值得进一步验证的线索。例如，Tsc1 和 Tsc2 是共同参与调控细胞生长、代谢等过程的两个基因，但研究发现，在小脑部分神经元中，干预 Tsc2 会改变多种与神经元通信有关的基因表达，而干预 Tsc1 并未产生同等程度的变化。这一差异可能有助于研究人员进一步理解结节性硬化症相关的脑部异常。另一条线索涉及与神经退行性疾病有关的 DCTN1 基因。研究发现，干预该基因后，部分与胆固醇合成有关的基因表达水平上升。AI 智能体将这一现象与既有文献中有关胆固醇运输异常的研究联系起来，并提出一个待验证的问题：DCTN1 功能异常是否会影响神经元内部的胆固醇分布，并进一步参与神经退行性变化。研究团队还对分布式智能体与单个智能体的表现进行了盲测比较。在 20 组配对报告中，生物学专家在 75% 的评审中更倾向于分布式智能体生成的报告；单个智能体的报告获得 16.7% 的评审偏好，其余 8.3% 的评审结果为平局。研究人员称，随着分析任务规模扩大，分布式架构也能检索和引用更多科学文献。在最大规模的测试中，分布式智能体引用了 700 多篇文献，而单个智能体仅引用 11 篇。相关研究论文已于 2026 年 10 月 16 日发布在 bioRxiv 预印本平台，目前尚未经过同行评审。研究团队强调，AI 提出的生物学联系和作用机制仍属于有待验证的研究假设，后续仍需通过实验确认。相关推理图谱、分析流程和代码已向研究人员开放，可用于探索基因干预结果、比较不同细胞类型的反应，并筛选值得优先开展实验的研究方向。IT之家附论文地址：https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.10.15.759436v1相关阅读：《OpenAI 联手 PerturbAI：让近 2000 个 AI 智能体一起搞科研，加速新药研发》

articles.title: 中国科学家在地球深处发现隐藏氧气来源：高压实验显示硅酸盐熔体可储存超 5% 额外氧
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，地球大气中的氧气从何而来，绝大部分人都会说光合作用。但一项新研究提出，在地球历史的某个关键节点，岩浆本身可能也曾充当过重要的氧气搬运工。中国学者发表在《国家科学评论》上的一项高压实验与模拟研究显示，硅酸盐熔体在高压下能够容纳远超传统化学计量预期的“额外氧”，这些氧随岩浆上升、压力降低而被逐步释放，为理解约 25 亿至 20 亿年前大气氧含量的第一次大幅上升提供了一条此前未被纳入考量的深部路径。传统上，地球科学家计算岩浆中的氧含量，依据的是硅、镁、铁等主要元素的丰度和价态。氧在硅酸盐地幔中占原子总数的一半以上，但绝大部分被化学键固定，其数量被认为完全由这些阳离子的“配方”决定。与水和二氧化碳不同，氧本身长期不被视为一种可以独立溶解在岩浆中的挥发性组分。由北京高压科学研究中心（HPSTAR）林彦好研究员与毛河光院士领衔，联合西北工业大学牛海洋教授及阿姆斯特丹自由大学 Wim van Westrenen 教授的团队，对这一默认假设进行了直接检验。研究团队在实验室中合成了洋中脊玄武岩，在 1200 至 1800 摄氏度、1 个大气压至 7 吉帕斯卡的范围内进行熔融实验。7 吉帕斯卡约相当于 100 万磅每平方英寸的压力，接近上地幔的部分条件。为制造富氧环境，他们在部分样品中加入了氧化铂，随后将熔体快速冷却为玻璃，并测量其元素组成、水含量和二氧化碳含量，从中剥离出“化学计量必需氧”与“挥发分中的氧”，剩余部分被定义为“额外氧”。结果呈现出清晰的压强依赖：在 1 个大气压下，额外氧接近于零；当压力升至 7 吉帕斯卡时，额外氧超过了样品重量的 5%，精确值为 5.2 ± 0.2 wt.%。作为对照，未添加氧化铂的同等温压实验仅产出 0.2% 至 0.5 wt.% 的额外氧。一个关键问题是，这些多出来的氧究竟进入了熔体结构，还是仅仅以气泡形式被物理包裹。拉曼光谱检测未在玻璃中发现氧气的气态信号，表明额外氧已被结合进硅酸盐网络之中。牛海洋团队基于深度神经网络原子间势的模拟进一步解释了这一容纳机制：随着氧含量升高，氧原子的电荷分布范围变宽，其中一小部分氧原子彼此之间形成了过氧化物型的键。模拟采用的简化镁-硅-氧体系给出的绝对氧含量低于玄武岩实验，但同样复现了氧储量随压力上升的趋势。由于部分氧可能在淬火过程中逃逸，实验测得的 5% 量级很可能只是熔体实际储存能力的下限。这一发现的意义延伸到地表。在氧化性较强的地幔区域形成的岩浆，可以在深处装载大量额外氧；当它向上运移、压力下降时，熔体的储氧能力随之降低，过剩的氧便会被释放出来，氧化浅部地幔、地壳和大气。研究作者指出，这一机制与地质记录中的一个时间重叠形成了呼应：大气氧含量在约 25 亿至 20 亿年前的大氧化事件（GOE）期间显著上升，而一些规模最大的大火成岩省（LIPs）也恰好在相近的时间窗口大规模喷发。基于实验数据的粗略估算显示，如果那一时期喷发的岩浆仅释放出其重量 0.27% 的额外氧，就足以供应今天整个大气层中所含的氧气总量。这一数字与实验在 7 吉帕斯卡下测得的储氧能力相比并不苛刻，但需要注意的是，0.27% 是基于全球规模岩浆活动的量级推演，并非对某一次具体喷发的直接测量，其与实际地质过程的吻合程度仍有待后续工作检验。IT之家附论文地址：https://doi.org/10.1093/nsr/nwag539

articles.title: 比亚迪第二代海豹 07 内饰官图，采用全新设计语言
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，比亚迪今日发布了第二代海豹 07 内饰官图，新车采用了全新设计语言，除了保留大尺寸悬浮中控屏和液晶仪表外，方向盘、中控台装饰、出风口造型均有所变化。据介绍，该车搭载奢享舒适座椅，支持零重力、按摩、通风、加热等功能，拥有同级最大后排空间，配备 20 扬帝瓦雷音响。此前，比亚迪汽车海洋网销售事业部总经理张卓已公布第二代海豹 07 的外观，新车的定位将是 C 级全享家轿。相比现款车型，新车前脸拥有大量锋利的线条，采用全新样式的日行灯组，显得更加“凶猛”；侧面则采用类似溜背的轮廓，张力十足。细节方面，新车还配备半隐藏式门把手和车顶激光雷达。IT之家注意到，新车已于 8 月登陆工信部申报名单，车身尺寸为长 5080mm /宽 1960mm /高 1495mm，轴距达到 2960mm，额定载客 5 人，提供纯电、插混两种动力版本可选。纯电版本搭载由西安比亚迪汽车零部件有限公司生产的永磁同步驱动电机，提供两种动力版本：低功率版本峰值功率 245kW，额定功率 115kW，整备质量 1975kg；高功率版本峰值功率 300kW，额定功率 150kW，整备质量 2060kg。纯电车型电池均采用磷酸铁锂蓄电池，由弗迪电池相关企业生产，最高车速可达 240km/h。

articles.title: 微星神影 16 魔龙姬星际套装体验：锐龙 9 8940HX ，纯白高颜值与硬核性能兼得
articles.content: 对于游戏本来说，性能往往是选购时最先考虑的因素，但外观同样影响着日常使用体验。尤其是高性能游戏本，常见设计大多强调硬朗的机身线条与浓厚的电竞风格。如果想找一款性能足够强、外观又不那么浮夸张扬的产品，市面上的选择并不算多。就在近日，IT之家拿到了一款特殊的游戏本新品 —— 神影 16 魔龙姬星际套装 2026。作为微星 40 周年推出的特别产品，它将二次元 IP「魔龙姬」融入神影系列的设计之中，以「星云白」配色取代常见的黑灰色机身，让游戏本有了不同于传统电竞风格的表达。这款产品曾在 Computex 2026 上亮相，此次我们也有机会对它进行实际体验。值得一提的是，本次IT之家拿到的并不只有笔记本本体，还包括同主题耳机、鼠标和鼠标垫。从机身到外设，整套装备都融入了魔龙姬的设计元素，视觉风格保持统一。对于喜欢二次元文化的年轻用户，尤其是学生群体而言，这样一套装备既能满足游戏娱乐需求，也能为日常学习和桌面搭配增添一些个性。当然，限定版的看点并不止于外观。它搭载 AMD 锐龙 9 8940HX 处理器、115W 满功耗 RTX 5060 Laptop GPU，并配备一块 16 英寸 2.5K 分辨率、240Hz 刷新率的釉月屏。接下来，IT之家就从设计、硬件性能到实际游戏表现，全面体验这款微星神影 16 魔龙姬限定款锐龙版，看看它除了特别的外观之外，还有哪些值得关注的地方。一、设计星云白机身搭配魔龙姬元素，限定版设计颇具辨识度拿到微星神影 16 魔龙姬限定款，首先能感受到的变化来自外观。微星神影 16 魔龙姬限定款采用了星云白配色，并将微星旗下的二次元 IP「魔龙姬」融入整体设计。机身 A 面采用白色盖板，右侧布置了微星龙盾 Logo。表面的幻彩珠光涂层会随着光线和观察角度的变化，呈现出细微的色泽差异，让纯白机身多了几分层次感。整体线条依然保留了游戏本应有的硬朗感，而星云白配色则柔和了传统电竞设计的凌厉气质，让整机看起来更加清爽，也少了几分张扬。微星神影 16 魔龙姬限定款可以单手掀开屏幕，最大开合角度约为 135°。翻开机身，其配备了一块 16 英寸釉月屏，屏幕上边框中央集成了摄像头，旁边设置了物理防窥开关，并配有麦克风开孔。分辨率为 2560×1600（2.5K），16:10 比例，刷新率达到 240Hz，官方标称覆盖 100% DCI-P3 广色域、500nits 峰值亮度。IT之家通过校色仪对这块屏幕进行了实测。在默认设置下，实测屏幕峰值亮度约为 492.4cd/m²，与官方标称的 500nits 基本吻合，日常室内使用足够明亮。色域方面，实测这块屏幕覆盖：99.9% sRGB 色域覆盖、146.7% sRGB 色域容积87.2% AdobeRGB 色域覆盖、101.1% AdobeRGB 色域容积97.7% DCI-P3 色域覆盖、103.9% DCI-P3 色域容积可以看到，这块屏幕在 DCI-P3 广色域上的表现与官方标称基本一致，97.7% 的覆盖对于一款主打游戏的笔记本来说已经相当不错；sRGB 色域覆盖接近 100%，日常办公、网页浏览和视频播放的色彩表现也有保障。整体来看，这块 2.5K 240Hz 屏幕在分辨率、刷新率、色域和亮度之间取得了不错的平衡，无论是玩游戏还是日常办公、影音娱乐，都能提供足够细腻流畅的视觉体验。此外，微星也提供了“MSI True Color”应用，这是一款专业屏幕色彩管理软件，用户可通过软件主页面一键切换 sRGB、Adobe RGB 以及 Display P3 色域，每个色域还支持选项丰富的自定义调节。回到键盘部分。C 面的键盘区域延续了白色主题，采用带数字小键盘的全尺寸布局，下方搭配一块大尺寸一体式触控板。WASD 四个按键与电源键使用了半透明键帽设计，方便背光透出。方向键则加入了像素风格的网点渐变纹理，与魔龙姬限定版的个性化设计相呼应。键盘支持四分区 RGB 背光，可以通过 MSI Center 调整颜色和灯效。掌托区域的左下方贴有 AMD 锐龙 9 HX、GeForce RTX 和 HDMI 相关标识，右下方则加入了魔龙姬家族徽章，进一步强调限定版身份。触控板采用与机身一致的白色设计，表面略微下凹，横向延伸的布局也让整个掌托区域看起来更加舒展。机身尺寸方面，微星神影 16 魔龙姬限定款厚度约为 21.95–23.85mm，重量约 2.25kg。相比上一代产品，这次全新模具在体积上做了明显瘦身，配合白色机身，视觉上比传统厚重游戏本轻盈不少。日常塞入双肩背包带去图书馆、办公室，不会有太强烈的负担感，尽管谈不上轻薄，但在 16 寸高性能游戏本中也属于相对便携的水准了。接口布局上，微星神影 16 魔龙姬限定款将接口分布在机身左右两侧及后部。机身左侧设有锁孔、电源接口，以及两个 USB-

articles.title: 谷歌 YouTube、Chrome 推进 AV2 支持，压缩效率较 AV1 提升近 30%
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，开放媒体联盟（AOMedia）当地时间 10 月 22 日宣布，下一代视频编码标准 AV2 正在浏览器、流媒体平台及开发工具等领域加速推进。谷歌已展示 Chrome 浏览器播放 AV2 视频的能力，并确认 YouTube 网页版计划最早于 2027 年初开始提供 AV2 视频。AV2 标准于 2026 年 6 月正式发布，在压缩效率方面较 AV1 提升约 30%，能够在相同码率下提供更高画质，或在维持相近画质的情况下减少带宽占用。IT之家注：AV2 依然采用免版税的开放标准路线，由谷歌、亚马逊、苹果、英特尔、Meta、Netflix、三星、腾讯等头部企业参与开发。谷歌已展示 Chrome 中 AV2 视频播放能力，而 YouTube 工程总监 Des Keane 则表示，YouTube 希望通过开放编码格式，在减少播放中断的同时提供更好的画质，并利用 AV2 的多视频能力支持新的观看体验。AOMedia 公布的数据显示，截至 2026 年 3 月 19 日，按观看时长加权计算，YouTube 视频库中已有超过 90% 的内容支持 AV1。谷歌预计，AV2 将在此基础上进一步提升视频传输效率，并为多路视频同时播放等功能提供支持。除了常规在线视频播放，AV2 还针对实时通信、沉浸式媒体、更高帧率和 HDR 高动态范围视频进行了优化。其多视频流和多视角支持能力，也有望应用于多摄像机画面、分屏视频以及视频会议等场景。Netflix 和亚马逊 Prime Video 目前也在评估 AV2。AOMedia 表示，联盟成员正推进编码器和解码器开发、标准符合性测试、性能基准测试、互操作性验证、内容制作工具以及硬件适配等工作。这些环节将影响 AV2 在不同浏览器、终端设备和流媒体平台上的实际部署进度。此前的 AV1 标准已经在 YouTube 等平台得到应用，但另一项视频编码标准 VVC（H.266）的普及速度相对有限，AV2 最终能否获得更广泛的产业支持，仍有待后续发展验证。相关阅读：《AV2 v1.0.0 视频编码标准发布：完整规范已公开，硬件支持可能还要等几年》《压缩效率提升约 30%，新一代 AV2 视频编码标准正式发布》

articles.title: 小米公益基金会驰援西藏那曲地震救灾
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，小米公益基金会紧急联动备灾伙伴 @中国红十字基金会 @北京新阳光慈善基金会 驰援西藏那曲地震救灾，助力受灾群众早日恢复正常生活。IT之家附小米原文如下：小米公益基金会联动备灾伙伴驰援西藏那曲地震救灾2026 年 10 月 22 日晚，西藏那曲市巴青县发生 7.0 级地震，造成重大人员伤亡。国务院抗震救灾指挥部办公室、应急管理部已将国家地震灾害应急响应提升至三级。小米公益基金会迅速响应应急管理部政社协同保障机制，第一时间启动应急响应，联动中国红十字基金会、北京新阳光慈善基金会快速开展一线救援协同与应急生活物资保障工作。联合中国红十字基金会捐赠的 400 件矿泉水及 1000 件方便面，已于今晚连夜启运灾区；联合北京新阳光慈善基金会捐赠的 500 个救灾安置箱，将于 24 日启运巴青县，为受灾群众提供紧急支持。我们将持续关注灾情动态，依据当地需求，协同备灾伙伴持续做好物资调运与救助支持，助力受灾群众早日恢复正常生活。守望相助，西藏安康！相关阅读：《美团驰援西藏巴青地震灾区，首批救灾物资已紧急启运》《字节跳动公益基金会驰援西藏那曲，首批应急物资已发往灾区》《驰援西藏那曲地震灾区，阿里巴巴首批物资已发出》《西藏那曲市巴青县发生 7.0 级地震，中国移动、联通、电信紧急驰援》《西藏那曲发生 7.0 级地震，苹果 CEO 特努斯宣布 Apple 将捐款支持在当地开展救援工作的组织》

articles.title: 美团驰援西藏巴青地震灾区，首批救灾物资已紧急启运
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，据美团公益官方公众号，西藏那曲市巴青县发生 7.0 级地震。灾情发生后，美团公益基金会迅速响应应急管理部应急物资政社协同保障机制，紧急启动突发公共事件应急响应机制，携手壹基金驰援西藏那曲地震受灾地区。10 月 22 日 22 时 33 分，西藏那曲市巴青县发生 7.0 级地震。截至 10 月 23 日 13 时，地震已造成 16 人遇难、76 人受伤。23 日凌晨，国家防减救灾委、应急管理部启动国家自然灾害救助四级应急响应；23 日上午，国务院抗震救灾指挥部办公室、应急管理部将国家地震灾害应急响应提升至三级。灾情发生后，美团公益基金会迅速响应应急管理部应急物资政社协同保障机制，紧急启动突发公共事件应急响应机制，携手壹基金驰援西藏那曲地震灾区。针对高海拔地区防寒保暖的迫切需求，美团公益基金会首批联合壹基金调集的救灾物资已紧急启运，包括棉帐篷 50 顶、应急食品 5000 盒、棉被 500 床，支持受灾群众过渡安置和基本生活保障。相关阅读：《字节跳动公益基金会驰援西藏那曲，首批应急物资已发往灾区》《驰援西藏那曲地震灾区，阿里巴巴首批物资已发出》《西藏那曲市巴青县发生 7.0 级地震，中国移动、联通、电信紧急驰援》《西藏那曲发生 7.0 级地震，苹果 CEO 特努斯宣布 Apple 将捐款支持在当地开展救援工作的组织》

articles.title: 苹果总市值盘初升至 5.12 万亿美元，暂时超越英伟达位居全球榜首
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，得益于 iPhone Duo 全球首销获得的佳绩，美股开盘后，苹果公司总市值直线飙升至 5.12 万亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 34.24 万亿元人民币），超过英伟达的 5.10 万亿美元，暂时位居全球上市公司市值榜首。行情数据显示，苹果股价上涨 0.84%，报 351.132 美元 / 股；英伟达股价下跌 0.19%，报 211.800 美元 / 股。受两家公司股价变动影响，苹果总市值短暂领先英伟达。苹果此前已于 2026 年 10 月 14 日首次在美股收盘时站上 5 万亿美元市值关口，成为继英伟达之后第二家达到这一水平的公司。今年 7 月，苹果也曾在盘中短暂超过英伟达，成为全球市值最高的公司，但此后英伟达重新夺回榜首。

articles.title: 长鑫科技：对全球和中国 DRAM 产业中长期前景保持坚定信心
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，据《科创板日报》今日报道，记者今日从长鑫科技方面了解到，从中长期看，AI 对数据吞吐的需求仍在迅速增长，DRAM 作为战略性基础设施的地位将会更加强化；中国作为全球最大的半导体应用市场，提升 DRAM 自给能力也具有重要的现实意义，发展空间广阔。其表示，“这是一个需要耐心、需要长期主义、需要永葆创业精神的行业。我们对全球和中国 DRAM 产业的中长期前景，保持坚定信心。”据IT之家此前报道，长鑫科技于 2025 年 10 月宣布量产 LPDDR5X 产品，芯片形态提供了覆盖 12GB、16GB、24GB 等多个容量点的解决方案，模组形态的 LPCAMM 产品容量为 16GB 和 32GB。今年 9 月，长鑫存储官宣自主研发的 LPDDR6 芯片已实现量产商用，首发搭载于小米 18 Fold 折叠旗舰手机。长鑫科技 10 月 16 日发布 2026 年前三季度（2026 年 1 月～2026 年 9 月）业绩预告报告：营业总收入：2650 亿元 ~2700 亿元，同比预增 725.96%~741.54%归母净利润：1310 亿元 ~1325 亿元，同比扭亏为盈长鑫科技此前在公告中表示，2025 年下半年以来 AI 算力需求快速增长，全球 DRAM 行业景气度大幅提升，产品供不应求、价格大幅上涨；公司稳步推进产能建设、产品研发和工艺技术提升，单位晶圆产出和产能利用率持续提高，规模效应逐步显现；同时公司优化运营管理、拓展市场，深化产业链上下游协同，推动业务规模快速扩张，推动整体业绩显著提升。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 23 日消息，长城汽车宣布旗下 2027 款坦克 500 正式上市，新车共推出 4 款车型，售价 33.5 万元起，IT之家整理价格信息如下：2027 款坦克 500车型售价（万元）Hi4-T33.5Hi4-T 智享版35.53.0T35.5Hi4-Z 智享版37.5新款坦克 500 新增“丹霞红”车色，取色于中国丹霞地貌亿万年沉积而成的赤壁丹崖，以“沉赤如岩，红而不喧”的暗调质感，演绎不张扬却自带气场的高级感。该车前脸配备大尺寸前格栅，格栅内部搭载横向镀铬饰条，整车设计灵感取自山川地貌与中国古建筑。侧面配备密辐式轮圈、车顶行李架，车窗边缘设置镀铬饰条，采用传统结构车门把手。内饰方面，2027 款车型新增全新黑灰配色，以玄黑为底、雅灰铺陈，展现出东方水墨般的虚实层次。车辆搭载 15.6 英寸中控双联屏，配合两侧副驾头枕音响与近场定向发声技术，实现主副驾功能分区、声场独立；全车配有 22 扬声器；带有 NAPPA 真皮座椅，均配备通风、加热、按摩功能。智能化方面，2027 款坦克 500 带有激光雷达、前向 4D 毫米波雷达在内的 27 个辅助驾驶传感器，搭载 Coffee Pilot 4 辅助驾驶系统，配合 Thor-U 高算力芯片，号称能够精准识别旁侧盲区、路口鬼探头、窄路通行等潜在风险，提前减速预留避险空间。规格方面，该车长宽高分别为 5078/1934/1905mm，轴距 2850mm；接近角 29°，离去角 24°，最小离地间隙 210mm。车辆提供三种版本动力，其中 Hi4-T 版本搭载 2.0T 发动机 + 单电机 +9HAT 变速箱，系统综合功率 310kW，电池容量 37.1kWh，WLTC 工况纯电续航 110km，匹配非解耦四驱，面向越野场景；Hi4-Z 版本搭载 2.0T 发动机 + 双电机 +3 挡 DHT 变速箱，系统综合功率 635kW，电池容量 59.05kWh，WLTC 工况纯电续航 201km，定位泛越野使用；燃油版搭载 3.0T 涡轮增压发动机 +48V 轻混系统，匹配 9AT 变速箱，最大功率 260kW，峰值扭矩 500N·m。

Abstract: Scaling data, diversity and model capacity has improved embodied learning in physical environments, where diverse experiences remain grounded in shared physical laws. Abstract: LLM-driven evolutionary search is a promising paradigm for scientific discovery, but existing methods remain costly and slow, often applying expensive reasoning uniformly while underusing evidence from failed, redundant, and saturated trials. Lightweight models power both parallel Speculators, which generate and refine candidate programs, and an Advisor, which distills accumulated successes, failures, and saturated directions into persistent guidance for subsequent exploration. articles.title: Automating ML for Science: Can Frontier Agents Climb Scientific Hills in the Wild?
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28763v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Frontier coding agents are increasingly framed as end-to-end automated researchers, and ML for science offers a demanding test of that promise: improving a scientific model often requires domain insight beyond routine ML engineering. We introduce Agent4Sci, a long-horizon testbed for measuring how far today's agents can improve the published best models on scientific ML benchmarks, spanning 20 benchmarks across 11 domains. Rather than ranking agents on a leaderboard, Agent4Sci asks what kinds of progress agents can make on these tasks under in-the-wild conditions, and where they fall short. Empirically, today's frontier agents advance the published best on every benchmark, with Claude Opus reaching 10.4% mean relative improvement and no run flagged for academic misconduct. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28815v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agentic harness evolution optimizes an agent's instructions, tools, and control flow by using its task execution experiences as evolving evidence. While more evolution tasks should intuitively improve performance, our preliminary study reveals a paradoxical failure mode: the performance of existing methods degrades as the task pool expands. Our further analysis demonstrates that this degradation stems from suboptimal evidence selection during optimization, as different evidence combinations lead to substantially different evolution outcomes. To address this issue, we propose Successive Scale Racing (SSR), a framework that adaptively searches for optimal evidence combinations in each evolution round. SSR constructs diverse evidence combinations based on the corresponding task quality and coverage, and efficiently races the resulting candidate harnesses under a small compute budget. articles.title: Decision language models as affordable and rapid alternatives to LLM judges of clinical generative AI
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28826v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated judges of clinical artificial intelligence (AI) outputs are necessary, but large language model (LLM) judges are costly and slow at scale. We compared Jev, a decision language model that returns structured judgments, with frontier and open-weight LLM judges in four use cases. On 118 pediatric answers, Jev's agreement with physicians' ordinal quality ratings (Gwet's AC2 0.50; expected score 0.53) matched or exceeded that of seven of 12 LLM judges, including frontier models, Claude Opus 5.5 (0.49) and GPT-6 (0.38). On physician-graded binary HealthBench criteria, Jev matched or exceeded four of six LLM judges. On MedHELM's open-ended tasks, Jev's agreement with a three-LLM jury approached or exceeded the jurors' internal agreement. On HealthBench Professional, Jev matched the benchmark's reference judge, GPT-5.4, on 91% of criteria (other judges, 91-93%). Frontier judges cost 73-294 times more than Jev and took 7-57 times longer.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.28855v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Progress on foundation model pretraining is gated by who can afford a trial, and relational pretraining is no exception. Recipes are developed inside individual labs, reported under private protocols, and do not accumulate. Speedrun leaderboards remove that barrier by decentralizing the search rather than the training run. The problem is fixed, the stack is open, entries are ranked by wall-clock time to a quality target, and one GPU is enough to hold the record. Which database to hold out decides whether the benchmark can resolve improvements at all, so we fix it by calibration, ranking six candidates by how sharply a 45-minute learning curve separates improvement from seed noise. Abstract: Large language models increasingly take part in extended conversations where they can both shape and be shaped by another party's views, yet most persuasion research measures only one side of that exchange. Abstract: Many social evaluations for multiagent systems study behaviors as they emerge from environments instead of systematically intervening in the environment to elicit such behaviors. Abstract: Deep research systems iteratively plan, gather evidence, synthesize, and revise, making end-to-end latency a key bottleneck for interactive use. Abstract: Frontier language-model agents excel at complex tasks, but high inference costs make transferring their capabilities to smaller models essential. Abstract: Persistent memory is a largely undefended surface for injection and poisoning, and the same risk limits memory sharing among agents. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30206v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models scale model capacity efficiently by activating a small subset of parameters per token. However, in long-context inference, memory remains a major bottleneck because the KV cache grows linearly with sequence length. Existing KV cache compression methods reduce this cost for dense transformers, but overlook a problem specific to MoE: KV eviction can change which experts are selected during answer generation, degrading the generation quality. We propose MoEZip, a routing-aware KV cache compression for sparse MoE language models. To estimate the sensitivity of expert routing to perturbation, we propose a novel metric based on the Fisher information matrix of routing distributions. MoEZip combines this metric with attention weights for routing-aware scoring of contexts. Abstract: LLMs can act as scientific agents using tools to consult specialists and run experiments. Yet specialist information must enter their context, generally as text, images, audio or video: a bottleneck between models with rich, high-dimensional representations. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30223v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used in competitive programming, and their outputs are sensitive to how a prompt is phrased. Prior work has compared prompt strategies for accuracy on competitive programming, but not for runtime speed, and has not situated the results against human performance. In an exploratory study of one prompt in each of nine styles on GPT-5.5 across three accuracy tasks from the International Olympiad in Informatics (IOI) and two NP-hard speed tasks, we found that no single prompt was best: the strongest prompt depended on the task type and on whether results were summarized by the mean or the median, suggesting that, at least for these tasks, prompt style should be matched to the objective rather than treated as universal. Abstract: Global warming and climate change are major catalysts for plant diseases, significantly affecting food production worldwide. Addressing this issue requires continuous monitoring and early detection of plant diseases. While recent advancements in deep learning offer potential solutions, most models demand high processing power and struggle to perform efficiently on low-end electronic hardware. Furthermore, many existing works focus on specific crop diseases, limiting their broader applicability. This paper presents a lightweight Group Equivariance Attention Network (GANet) designed for the prediction and monitoring of 38 types of plant diseases. GANet introduces a novel Group Attention block and Group-Wise Feature Fusion block, making it both sparse and efficient. articles.content:

Abstract: Medical artificial intelligence (AI) models are often shared without their training data, assuming this protects the patients who contributed them. However, a model can reveal whether a patient's records were used in training, a privacy breach known as a membership inference attack. This risk is usually reported as a cohort average, which can appear negligible while individual patients are almost certainly exposed. Identifying potentially vulnerable records before developing a production model could make privacy assessment more practical. We measured each patient's vulnerability to membership inference attack, across 7,789 models trained on six clinical datasets in four modalities, including two adapted pretrained medical models. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30231v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Visual mathematical reasoning can fail before reasoning begins: when a vision-language model (VLM) misreads a diagram, subsequent reasoning proceeds from false premises. This perceptual bottleneck is especially pronounced in smaller models, while accurate textual descriptions can substantially narrow the gap to larger models. Because obtaining such descriptions at inference requires additional annotation or model calls, we propose minimal-edit corrective on-policy distillation. Using reference figure descriptions and verified reference solutions as training-only information, a teacher scores incorrect student rollouts under a minimal-edit objective, and only teacher-disfavored tokens contribute to the corrective loss. Correct rollouts receive task-reward reinforcement learning. This preserves on-policy supervision while avoiding full-response imitation. Abstract: Muon updates matrix-valued parameters along approximately orthogonalized directions and often trains large language models faster than AdamW, yet it remains unclear when and why orthogonalization helps. Orthogonalization pays off when the gradient is far from low rank and its largest singular directions see high curvature. articles.title: SWE-VERIFIER: Selective Verification for Cost-Efficient Coding Agents
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30284v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding agents spend substantial computation generating actions and processing long interaction histories. Poor action choices can steer agents into low-value states, wasting computation and increasing API costs. Sampling and verifying alternative actions can improve the agent's decisions, but applying this procedure at every step adds substantial overhead. We introduce SWE-Verifier, a lightweight generative model that selectively triggers candidate sampling and verification. It scores the coding agent's proposed action to determine when additional candidate sampling is needed, then ranks the resulting actions before execution. We train SWE-Verifier from Qwen3.5-4B using preference data that groups contrasting actions with their resulting environment observations and rubric-guided teacher scores. articles.content:

Abstract: A fundamental challenge in Bayesian network structure learning lies in efficiently approximating the posterior distribution of directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). For large, high-dimensional datasets, the task remains beyond the capabilities of current methods. This work advances Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms by introducing novel moves that simultaneously resample the parents for multiple nodes of the DAG. At the core of these moves is duet sampling, a new generalization of the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm that selects two proposal distributions from a pool at each iteration. articles.content:

Abstract: In recent years, Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) have gained massive attention as an energy-efficient neural computing paradigm due to their event-driven and sparse computing capability. However, maintaining accuracy under low-precision constraints, necessary for practical deployment, has been largely unexplored for SNN models. In addition, existing Hessian-based approaches for quantization, such as HAWQ-V2, incur significant memory and computational overhead due to temporal unrolling across multiple SNN timesteps. Abstract: Long-horizon node outages are harder than conventional missing-value imputation because complete sensor trajectories remain unobserved for extended periods, while the usefulness of spatial and temporal dependencies varies across outage locations and operating regimes. Existing graph, diffusion, and flow-based methods typically impose a fixed structural bias, which can oversmooth abrupt changes or propagate errors from unreliable neighbors. A missing-only flow-matching backbone learns a conditional velocity field while keeping observed measurements exactly fixed. Abstract: Training Arabic large language models faces challenges from noisy web data, dialectal variation, and the high cost of continual pretraining (CPT). We introduce AQL-Lite (AQL: Arabic Quality Language), a time- and resource-efficient framework for adapting a multilingual LLM to Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). articles.title: Consistency Is Not Validity: Self-Rewarded Moral Argumentation Makes Language Models Decisive but Pliable
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30349v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLMs are increasingly consulted for moral judgment. We aim to improve performance on such tasks by rewarding good arguments, on the premise that arguing well increases the likelihood of judging well. We train a reinforcement learning policy initialized from a state-of-the-art language model in a self-judged tournament with masked thinking: the generated arguments are judged pairwise on argument quality by the policy itself. As an empirical basis, we extract authentic dilemmas from classic novels, using a logic solver to verify that each constitutes a conflict. We show that our judge rates argument quality like human annotators, and the policy then adopts the language register that it rewards. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30355v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Hallucinated citations make it harder to trace sources and verify the evidence behind scientific claims. Detecting them is difficult because bibliographic records can be incomplete or differ across source types and publication versions. A plausible match alone neither validates the citation nor establishes its underlying source. We introduce CiteResolve, a benchmark of 423 real-world hallucinated citations annotated for source recoverability. We further propose CiteAnchor, a source-aware grounding framework that adapts retrieval and field-level verification to each source type and separately determines citation validity and whether a unique source can be recovered. On an existing detection benchmark, CiteAnchor achieves 0.841 F1 with GPT-5.6 Luna and 0.784 with an open-weight backbone, outperforming the baseline with the same backbones by 7.9 and 36.8 points. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30379v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents are flexible in language interaction, but using them as long-horizon planners is costly and prone to hallucinated or invalid actions. This paper targets a different role for LLMs: constrained bridges between language and symbolic planning. We propose MemPlan, a memory-conditioned PDDL planning framework for partially observable interactive text environments. MemPlan keeps the PDDL domain fixed and reconstructs the PDDL problem at each step from parsed observations, candidate hypotheses, and interaction memory. Positive graph memory assigns relevance-based action costs to candidate hypotheses for missing objects, locations, or conditions, guiding the planner toward more plausible checks. Negative memory records execution-refuted assumptions and compiles them into exclusion constraints, preventing repeated attempts at candidates already contradicted by feedback. arXiv:2610.30412v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based chat agents are increasingly used for complex, multi-turn, multilingual medical triage in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet evaluation methods focus on single-turn, English-only benchmarks that primarily test the chatbots' knowledge. In practice, users are often confused, overwhelmed, or emotionally vulnerable, giving unclear, misspelled single-word answers or long messages in regional dialects, and the context of a conversation can shift rapidly. We propose SIM-UT (Simulation of User Behaviour for Triage), a multi-turn, simulation-based evaluation method that identifies ecologically valid, contextually relevant failure modes of LLM-based triage chat agents. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30435v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent advances in search agents have enabled large language models to tackle complex tasks by retrieving and synthesizing external information. However, existing search agents often lack search-state awareness, i.e., the ability to recognize what information has been obtained and what remains missing, leading to hallucinated reasoning and prematurely terminated search. To address this limitation, we propose Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning (SARL), a reinforcement learning framework in which models learn to recognize their own search state during training and improve their search behavior accordingly, without requiring additional assessment at test time. SARL achieves this through a dual reward design that captures the corrective effect of each assessment while penalizing excessive reliance on it, jointly encouraging effective and efficient search trajectories. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30504v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used to answer factual questions, but their answers can contain errors and must be fact-checked claim by claim. Yet the resulting score depends on three design decisions: which questions the claims answer, under what conditions each claim is judged, and which sources count as evidence. No existing benchmark specifies all three. We introduce JSFactCheckBench, a Japanese benchmark that specifies all three, with 1,913 claims from LLM answers to questions about misleading information that circulated on Japanese social media, each annotated for factuality at a reference time and for importance to the question, using evidence from preselected Web sources. articles.content:

Abstract: LLM judges are used to determine which of two answers is better. Trusting these verdicts requires knowing how repeatable they are and how much they depend on the judge's instructions. We show that similar aggregate scores can conceal substantial changes in individual verdicts, both when the same setup is repeated and when the instructions change. Using 500 Arena-Hard v2.0 prompts with two models' answers held fixed, we run GPT-4.1 as the judge under all eight combinations of criteria, output format and task framing, and repeat every setup unchanged at temperature zero on a pinned model version. Rerunning the default setup moves the aggregate score by about one point but changes the win/tie/loss outcome on 21.2% of prompts. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30518v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present Protegrity-PII, a new PII decision model for structured and unstructured text. Protegrity-PII achieves a typed recall of 0.915 with a precision of 0.907 on a new benchmark we propose, PII-SCOPE. Our model processes text in 0.49 seconds per million characters at \$0.0005 per million characters on a single RTX 6000 using batched inference. Due in part to the expansive nature of the entity type taxonomy used in training, Protegrity-PII achieves superior out-of-distribution generalization when benchmarked against a selection of state of the art models and datasets.

Abstract: Industry Foundation Classes (IFC), the standard for building information exchange in architecture, engineering, and construction (AEC), is increasingly queried through large language models (LLMs) using natural language. The taxonomy covers 15 categories and 36 subtypes across four groups, with answer keys derived from the file and distractors constructed from file-derived values or predefined rules. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30635v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coding-agent benchmarks often describe a task in natural language but grade it with tests taken from the upstream project. Passing those tests can require information the description never states: a constant's name, a module path, an exact message. We call this a specification-oracle gap: where it exists, a benchmark also measures whether an agent reproduces upstream implementation details. We formalise the gap, including the inconsistencies that chains of dependent tasks add, and build a static audit for five languages that classifies every name-, path- and literal-level dependency of every scored test (held-out precision 89.2%, recall 92.9%). On SWE-Milestone (98 graded milestones, 35 published runs), 25 milestones contain a test that depends on an unstated, non-inferable name or path. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30664v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models increasingly act as controllers in structured decision pipelines, yet their decisions are still executed by autoregressive text decoding. Hierarchical RAG is one such setting: at each frontier of a document tree, an LLM commits to $b$ of $k$ sections under an input-dependent action grammar, executed as either failure-prone free-form JSON or reliable but strictly serial grammar-constrained generation. We show that this serialization is unnecessary for bounded-horizon control: the reachable future forms a shallow action-prefix tree, which we compile --- one root prefill plus one tree-causal probe evaluate every prefix-conditioned action distribution with serial decoding's tokens, positions, and causal ancestry. Abstract: Singular-value spectra encode important structure in transformer feed-forward projections, yet their causal role in downstream behavior remains underexplored. articles.title: WikiOriginQA: Automated Construction of a QA Dataset with Knowledge Origins for Analyzing Cultural Bias
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30677v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Existing datasets on cultural knowledge have been typically created by human annotators familiar with each culture. However, the process requires considerable human effort, presenting a significant challenge to scalability. To address this challenge, we introduce WikiOriginQA, a QA dataset automatically constructed by objectively representing the origins of knowledge through the creation dates of different Wikipedia language editions. Experimental results with the created dataset confirm that LLM performance tends to be biased toward Anglophone cultures. Furthermore, the results suggest the importance of knowledge propagation into the Anglosphere. These findings demonstrate the validity of our automated approach, enabling cultural bias evaluations with superior scalability across diverse languages without extensive manual annotation.

Abstract: We study mountain-bike action quality assessment (AQA) with weak labels and candidate feedback. The training corpus comprises 95 field-recorded jump clips with binary labels denoting good or poor technique. These are coarse categorical labels, not continuous expert quality scores; phase-boundary and aspect-level annotations are unavailable. Abstract: We introduce EgoHand, a monocular 3D hand reconstruction model that achieves state-of-the-art performance on egocentric video. Central to our approach is the curation of a high-quality training corpus of 14 million images, combining synthetic data, in-the-wild video, and multi-camera motion capture to balance scene diversity and supervision quality. The model adopts SOMA-Hand as its parametric representation and processes 2D hand crops with a transformer encoder, incorporating camera cues and an auxiliary 2D branch to improve geometric consistency and image alignment. Zero-shot evaluations on HOT3D, ARCTIC, and H2O demonstrate strong out-of-domain generalization, with lower joint-position, root-translation, and acceleration errors than competing baselines at an inference latency of approximately 9.69 ms. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30337v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Generating an articulated object from a single image requires recovering both its appearance and the mechanism governing its parts. A compact encoding of joint attributes does not by itself ensure that reconstruction preserves the resulting motion. We present MoRE, Motion-Regularized Encoding for articulated 3D generation. MoRE represents coordinate-aligned joint lines with axis classification and two axis-orthogonal Pl\"ucker moment coefficients, removing the arbitrary choice of an origin along the axis. During representation learning, decoded joint hypotheses are used to move corresponding three-dimensional anchors, and their motions are compared with those of annotated joints. Abstract: We introduce Foundation4D, a unified feed-forward model for geometry estimation, 3D detection, semantic occupancy, and Gaussian reconstruction from multi-camera driving video. A shared backbone uses factorized spatiotemporal attention to efficiently combine observations across cameras and time. Our video inference pipeline uses pose graph optimization to refine camera trajectories and assembles object tracks across input windows. With benchmark-specific fine-tuning, Foundation4D achieves the lowest depth AbsRel on Waymo and nuScenes, the highest detection mAP on nuScenes, and the highest occupancy mIoU on OpenOccupancy among the compared methods. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30347v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose FiLM-CAM; a conditional-access image watermarking approach that enforces authorized encoding, decoding, and removal through keyed feature modulation. A secret key conditions a Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM) mechanism that transforms the internal representation of the watermark signal before embedding, thereby coupling the payload to the key at the feature, rather than pixel level. The same key must be presented to condition the decoder to correctly recover the payload embedded in an image. To enforce conditional access, we train the system to maximize the performance gap between authorized and unauthorized use, ensuring reliable extraction under the correct key while inducing failure under incorrect keys. In addition, we design our encoder to estimate the watermark residual invariant to the presence of pre-existing watermarks. articles.title: Latent Space Jam: Layout Guided Video Synthesis
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30390v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Adding control to video generation often requires training, which demands additional computational resources, data, or architectural changes. We propose a training-free approach that utilizes pretrained video diffusion models to control object layout and motion using coarse layouts. Our method operates in two passes: first, it steers spatiotemporal placement through prompt-guided cross-attention to produce a coarse visual guide; second, this guide conditions the same model to generate a high-quality, layoutconsistent video. The approach enables coordinated motion with strong temporal consistency, supporting diverse trajectories and object interactions without additional training. Extensive experiments show that our method consistently outperforms prior work in overlap and trajectory accuracy, as well as visual quality across static, dynamic, and multi-object scene settings.

articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30405v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern vision-based agents have shifted toward skill-based problem-solving, where a skill is an executable image-to-image operation, e.g., cropping, thresholding, or edge detection. As these skill libraries grow, they accumulate duplicated, mislabeled, and defective skills. The signals normally used to curate them (a skill's name, description, or source code) say little about how the skill visually changes the image. We present VisCurate, a framework and benchmark that curates visual skill libraries from observed execution rather than from text. VisCurate runs each candidate skill pair on a shared probe battery and assigns one of six behavioral relations, each tied to a library edit that is safe to make. The benchmark injects seven defect types into a clean library at controlled rates, producing 300 reproducible instances with ground-truth relations and repairs. Abstract: Reproducing a published 3DGS paper takes weeks of expert engineering before any extension can be proposed. Prior autonomous-research systems read papers, draft hypotheses, and write code, but are limited by short fixed templates, low executability, and weak traceability, and none has been demonstrated end-to-end in a live computer-vision subfield with intense activity. Abstract: LLMs have shown strong in-context learning (ICL) capability, but extending it to Multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) remains challenging. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30609v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have recently emerged as important remote sensing platforms, and UAV navigation has shown great potential in remote sensing applications. However, existing methods do not explicitly incorporate kinodynamic modeling or safety distances into trajectory generation, resulting in high absolute yaw rates, frequent collisions, and low navigation success rates, which limit safety and motion stability. To address this challenge, we introduce KinoUAV, a kinodynamic benchmark comprising a dataset and KinoUAV-Agent. First, we develop a hierarchical kinodynamic trajectory generation pipeline that drives UAV through acceleration actions. It uses waypoint chains from global planning and generates trajectories segment by segment under velocity, acceleration, and jerk constraints, reducing oscillations and improving trajectory stability. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30619v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Relighting and novel view synthesis of human portraits are essential in applications such as portrait photography, virtual reality (VR), and augmented reality (AR). Despite recent progress, 3D-aware portrait relighting remains challenging due to the demands for photorealistic rendering, real-time performance, and generalization to unseen subjects. Existing works either rely on supervision from limited and expensive light stage captured data or produce suboptimal results. Moreover, many works are based on generative NeRFs, which suffer from poor 3D consistency and low real-time performance. We resort to recent progress on generative 3D Gaussians and design a lighting model based on a unified neural radiance transfer representation, which responds linearly to incident light. arXiv:2610.30623v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) has shown superior performance in the image-level open-vocabulary classification task, benefiting from its powerful alignment of visual features and text embeddings. However, dense prediction tasks require models to perform pixel-level predictions, necessitating modifications to CLIP for region-text alignment. In this paper, we adjust the attention layers within the vanilla visual encoder of CLIP. With a novel attention calculation method for selective attention features, the model retains more regional semantic information. To further mitigate the negative impact of the modality gap, we introduce additional visual prototypes to refine the original predictor solely based on text embeddings. articles.title: FedBST: Bilateral Self-Training for Unsupervised Federated Classification
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30634v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Unsupervised federated learning with Vision-Language Models (e.g., CLIP) offers a promising solution for label-free classification, yet its performance often degrades under severe non-IID shifts. A pioneering method, FedCoPL, typically relies on self-training strategies that exclusively prioritize high-confidence predictions for pseudo-labeling. However, this selective approach neglects the information of ambiguous samples (often referred to as ``waist" samples), leading to the underutilization of data and biased decision boundaries. To address this limitation, we propose FedBST, a bilateral self-training framework that effectively exploits both high-confidence and ambiguous data. Specifically, for local optimization, we introduce uncertainty-aware confidence penalization (UACP). articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30639v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Self-supervised Vision Transformers learn strong image-level representations, but their patch-level representations can be unreliable for dense prediction. We study this mismatch and find that the class token concentrates global semantics on a small number of representative patches, while dense prediction errors often occur on low-attention regions. We provide a local gradient analysis showing that, along the [CLS] attention readout, image-level self-distillation gradients are weighted by [CLS]-to-patch attention mass. To provide masked patches with global semantics without changing the architecture, we propose Cross Distillation (CODI), which mixes a small amount of the teacher class-token distribution into each teacher patch-token target. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30643v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) requires agents to follow instructions and navigate to target locations. However, current VLN agents often suffer severe performance degradation in unseen environments due to distribution shifts. Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) offers a promising paradigm to bridge this gap, yet existing methods that rely on unsupervised entropy minimization can propagate errors through the trajectory, causing cascading failures in navigation. Recent methods mitigate this by incorporating human feedback, but they apply trajectory-level supervision uniformly across all steps without localizing the actions is truly informative, leading to inefficient feedback utilization and mismatched optimization granularity. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30646v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Federated unsupervised domain adaptation (FUDA) addresses the challenge of adapting models to an unlabeled target domain using decentralized source domains while preserving data privacy. However, existing FUDA methods typically require multiple communication rounds, rely on complex aggregation strategies, and often struggle with noisy pseudo labels and inconsistent source knowledge. To address these challenges, we propose SKD-ETR, a novel one-shot FUDA framework that combines Smoothed Knowledge Distillation (SKD) and Exponential moving average-based Teacher Refinement (ETR). SKD trains a student model on the target domain using smoothed soft pseudo labels generated by the ensemble of source models. This reduces overconfidence, mitigates noise, and improves robustness. articles.title: Residual Calibration via Local Feature-Space Refinement
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30652v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Deep neural networks often struggle to provide reliable confidence estimates, making post-hoc calibration essential for reliable decision-making. Existing post-hoc methods largely rely on score-based transformations, which improve marginal calibration but often fail to capture spatially varying miscalibration in local regions of the learned feature space. To address this gap, we propose Local Adaptive Probability Estimation (LAPE), a post-hoc residual calibration framework. Specifically, LAPE treats the global calibrator output as a stable anchor and refines the individual prediction by leveraging non-parametric local evidence from neighboring calibration samples. As a plug-and-play refinement module, LAPE effectively utilizes the information about feature-space geometry and can reuse the calibration data that are used to construct the global calibrator. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30197v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into embodied robotic planning, yet standard benchmarks primarily evaluate end-to-end task completion in nominal environments, obscuring failure origins across the execution stack. We present Alpha, a systematic fault-injection and robustness-evaluation framework for LLM-driven manipulation in simulation. Alpha injects calibrated faults across perception (sensor lag), actuation (grip slip), kinematics (unreachable targets), and planning (planner-output corruption), alongside concurrent conditions. To separate physical vulnerabilities from planner sensitivities, we introduce a matched methodology pairing an LLM agent (Llama-3 via Ollama) against a deterministic Scripted Oracle planner across a balanced 150-episode matrix under identical seeds, geometries, and safety criteria. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30319v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: End-to-end autonomous driving has achieved state-of-the-art performance on benchmarks and real-world deployments. Its standard training recipe, however, is expensive across all existing paradigms: imitation learning requires fleet-scale driving logs whose behavior distribution only thinly covers the safety-critical tail; closed-loop reinforcement learning in a photorealistic simulator, while offering diverse behaviors, is bottlenecked by sample-efficiency, per-step cost of rendering, and a forward pass through a large vision backbone. Self-play in vectorized simulators changes the economics: at millions of rollout steps per second, one can obtain a state distribution with natural diversity in collisions, near-misses, and recoveries that no driving log contains, and a highly reactive policy emerges from a basic driving-quality reward. Abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising approach to learning generalist robot policies using rich spatiotemporal priors from pre-trained video diffusion models. A recent line of WAMs improves inference efficiency by conditioning a separate action decoder on intermediate future video representations extracted from a single denoising step, avoiding costly iterative denoising required for video generation. This design makes action prediction depend directly on the quality of these future representations. In this paper, we introduce Future REpresentation learning via self-Distillation with temporal context (FRED), a framework that trains WAMs to improve the quality of future video representations from noise in a single denoising step. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30334v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Designing and tuning reward functions remains one of the main challenges in building effective reinforcement learning (RL) pipelines for humanoid locomotion. While shaping rewards can accelerate learning, naively formulated terms often conflict with the desired behavior, overfit to a specific robot, or become unstable under small weight changes. Potential-Based Reward Shaping (PBRS) offers an alternative solution: shaping the reward via differences of a potential function to guide exploration without changing the optimal policy. In this paper, we study Multi-PBRS for humanoid locomotion and propose a unified reward configuration. We then evaluate the same reward structure and weights across nine humanoid robots, requiring only robot-specific metadata (joint/link mappings and default poses) rather than per-robot reward redesign. articles.content:

Abstract: This paper presents an integrated control framework for high-speed platooning of articulated vehicles, combining advanced longitudinal and lateral control strategies to address the challenges of safe and efficient autonomous driving. A novel proof of string stability for the proposed longitudinal control algorithm, based on a PID framework, ensures robust inter-vehicle distance regulation even under dynamic operating conditions. Additionally, an arc-length-based longitudinal error formulation enhances the applicability of the control system for curved roads, making it realistic for diverse driving scenarios. For lateral control, significant improvements to the clothoid-based path tracking algorithm are introduced to mitigate oscillations and enhance stability at high speeds. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30438v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tactile sensing provides robots with direct access to physical interactions at the contact interface, making it a critical modality for robust and dexterous manipulation. Over the past several decades, tactile-based manipulation research has evolved from mechanics-driven approaches, which explicitly interpret tactile signals through contact mechanics and task-specific reasoning, to data-driven approaches that learn tactile representations and manipulation policies directly from data. This paper reviews the development of tactile-based manipulation from these two complementary perspectives. We first introduce the fundamentals of tactile sensing, and then review, from a mechanics-driven perspective, how those signals form manipulation-relevant state representations and subsequently influence the robot action. articles.title: Integrated Respiratory Sensing and Gated Control for Autonomous Needle Insertion Via CT Bore Robotic Arm
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30452v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Currently, CT-guided lung biopsy is a highly manual procedure requiring patient breath-holding, iterative manual needle insertions, and repeated CT confirmation scans to accurately target a tumor. Automating this process within the CT bore--without relying on manual needle placement or patient breath-holding--has the potential to reduce procedure time, patient discomfort, and radiation exposure. In this work, we present an integrated sensing and control system capable of performing a gated needle insertion within the CT bore. The experiments demonstrate the system's ability to track and predict patient breath cycles, perform autonomous respiratory-gated needle insertion, and detect breath cycle anomalies.

articles.title: PhysibleMDM: Enforcing Inference-Time Physical Feasibility Constraints on Motion Diffusion Models via Noise Optimization
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30500v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Motion Diffusion Models (MDMs) can generate diverse and visually appealing human motion; yet, the resulting trajectories frequently violate physical constraints, limiting their downstream use in simulation and control. We present PhysibleMDM, a framework that promotes physical feasibility of MDM output by optimizing at inference time the diffusion noise without retraining the generative model. We introduce a set of surrogate feasibility constraints that can be evaluated without full trajectory simulation. These constraints combine kinematic checks (e.g., ground penetration, slip, and self-collision) with dynamic feasibility tests computed via an inverse-dynamics inner loop formulated as a cone program. We solve the resulting black-box noise optimization problem using the Separable Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (Sep-CMA-ES), thereby avoiding reliance on computationally expensive and discontinuous gradients. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30528v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Predicting surrounding vehicles' lane-change intentions enables autonomous vehicles to anticipate potential hazards and respond proactively rather than relying solely on reactive maneuvers. This study investigates the benefits of integrating lane-change prediction, based on knowledge graph embeddings and Bayesian inference, into autonomous vehicle decision-making. Three driving strategies are evaluated in risky merging scenarios simulated in CARLA: reactive driving, prediction-based longitudinal action, and prediction-based lateral action. The proposed prediction model anticipates the surrounding vehicle's lane change approximately 3-4 seconds before its occurrence, allowing the ego vehicle to adjust its behavior accordingly. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30540v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Human motion retargeting bridges the embodiment gap between humans and humanoid robots by converting human demonstrations into reference trajectories for whole-body control and loco-manipulation. For object-interaction tasks, successful execution depends on accurately preserving body--object relations at critical stages. However, uniform per-frame iteration budgets do not account for these localized accuracy requirements, limiting the computational efficiency of retargeting. To address this limitation, we present Spatiotemporal Retargeting (STR), which uses keyframes and key body parts to allocate optimization effort. Specifically, a vision-language model selects relevant motion signals and body parts, and keyframes are identified from changes in the selected signals. articles.content:

Abstract: Recent advances in foundation-model agents have enabled increasingly capable embodied systems for long-horizon planning and interaction. However, embodied agents require fast, closed-loop decisions as they continuously perceive and act on a changing environment. Deploying strong cloud agents leaves the platform idle for seconds between consecutive actions, while lightweight local models respond quickly but are more vulnerable to errors. Existing hierarchical architectures typically assign models fixed roles, whereas conventional model routers make stateless per-request decisions. We present CARE, a critic-guided adaptive execution framework that dynamically determines when to escalate control from a local executor to a stronger cloud model. articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30589v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reliable robotic mapping in dynamic real-world environments is essential for embodied intelligence and long-term autonomy. However, existing methods often involve a trade-off: lightweight online mapping is efficient but captures limited semantic context, while dense mapping provides richer semantics at higher computational cost and is more vulnerable to distractors. They also struggle to relocalize objects after scene changes. To address these challenges, we propose the Online Anchor-centric Scene Inference System (OASIS), a unified system for online mapping, complex open-vocabulary retrieval, and navigation in dynamic environments. Abstract: Traversability estimation is critical for ground vehicle teleoperation, yet existing methods often neglect the human operator's preferences for speed and risk tolerance. articles.content:

Abstract: Dynamic interactive object search in large-scale human environments presents substantial challenges for existing methods. Current scene representations like 3D Scene Graphs (3DSG) only provide coarse-grained spatial segmentation and cannot identify functional areas such as storage or leisure areas. Without functional area understanding, existing methods are constrained to exhaustive sequential exploration at large scales, resulting in inefficient search behaviors -- particularly in open-layout environments with numerous interactive objects such as drawers and cabinets. Moreover, these methods lack adaptability to environmental dynamics such as object relocations. articles.title: Continuous-Time Motion Planning and Steering with Global Convergence
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30607v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Motion planning is central to robotics, and it is increasingly used to correct the motions proposed by learned planners and policies. In both uses, constraints must hold at every instant of the motion, not only at sampled times. To our knowledge, no algorithm provably converges to a globally optimal motion once a smoothness cost is combined with such constraints. We cast planning and steering as a single continuous-time program: robots avoid one another and static or moving obstacles, and a learned proposal is steered by keeping the motion close to it. The program is elementary to state, yet nonconvex. We propose GlobMP (Global Motion Planning), a gradient projection method over piecewise-polynomial curves, on which each constraint is one polynomial per piece that must stay nonnegative over the whole motion; it alternates cost reduction with feasibility restoration. articles.title: Co^2Gen: Collaboratively Generating Task Plans for Decentralized Multi-Robot and Human Collaboration
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30671v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Visual Language Action (VLA) models are designed to be generalist robot models that can be implemented across embodiments, tasks and environments. However, their ability to collaborate with other robots and humans remains underexplored. In this work, we propose a framework to automate the generation of multi-robot collaborative data for decentralized VLA training without requiring human teleoperation. Our framework first utilizes a decentralized collaborative planning approach to generate multi-robot collaborative robot plans in the form of an executable function. We then utilize the collaborative plan to produce collaborative demonstration data to finetune VLA models in a decentralized manner. We show that our approach produces demonstration data that when used to finetune VLA models on decentralized collaboration tasks matches the task performance of VLA models finetuned on human-teleoperated collaborative data.

Abstract: Autonomous robotic surgery has drawn increased attention in recent years due to its potential to relieve surgeons of time-consuming, mentally straining, and tedious tasks, particularly during prolonged operations. One suitable task for automation is suturing, which involves tracking the thread as it deforms during needle retrieval, de-tangling, knot tightening, and other tasks. articles.title: When One Step Is Enough: An Empirical Study of Euler Integration in Flow-Matching Policies
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30735v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Flow matching is now the dominant approach for vision-language action (VLA) robot policies, thanks to its expressiveness and simple training objective. However, inference for standard flow matching requires iteratively solving an ODE, limiting the control frequency at deployment. While several works have proposed novel methods to allow for single-shot action generation, we ask whether such additional objectives are actually necessary. We find that across six flow matching VLAs, one-step action generation largely matches multi-step sampling at scale: multi-step integration confers little to no consistent advantage at inference. We empirically find that this holds as long as models are sufficiently trained and have enough capacity. Practically, the implication is that for large VLAs, the single-step policy comes essentially for free from the multi-step model, enabling low-latency deployment without retraining, distillation, or auxiliary ob

articles.title: Causal Analysis of Failures of Cyber-Physical Systems with Continuous Inputs
articles.content:
arXiv:2610.30737v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern autonomous Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs), such as self-driving cars, operate in increasingly complex environments while expected to maintain high reliability. The black-box nature of many of these systems makes it impossible to fully verify their behavior prior to deployment. When a failure occurs, it is important to analyze it to guide improvements to system robustness. A recent work introduced the novel concept of leveraging the framework of actual causality for CPS failure explanation. However, that work considered only a discrete, binary causal model that cannot capture continuous changes in system inputs. In this paper, we address these limitations by extending the actual causality framework with the notion of distance to account for the continuous characteristics of the system. articles.title: A Unified Framework for Image-to-3D Part Generation via Variable Granularity
articles.content: Controllable 3D part generation is pivotal for digital asset creation, yet existing methods lack the flexibility to accommodate diverse user workflows requiring varying levels of control. In this paper, we introduce FlexPart, a unified image-to-3D part generation framework that supports variable-granularity geometric conditions within a single model. By seamlessly integrating heterogeneous inputs, ranging from sparse points to dense bounding boxes and masks, via gated adaptive modulation, FlexPart unlocks a powerful cross-modal synergy. We also propose an asymmetric geometric guidance mechanism that leverages strong spatial priors to align representations across granularities, improving geometric consistency and facilitating inter-task synergy. Under mask conditioning on PartVerseXL, FlexPart reduces Part CD by 16.6% relative to TripoSG + SAM3D and by 10.5% relative to OmniPart, while maintaining competitive whole-mesh quality. The code can be found at https://github.com/Gucci233/FlexPart

articles.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
articles.content: Robotic foundation models are typically evaluated through costly closed-loop rollouts, which motivates cheap offline proxies for model capability. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) suggests that as representations improve, different modalities such as vision and language converge toward a shared statistical model of reality. We ask whether motion trajectories form another such modality: as embodied models become more capable, should their sensory representations converge toward the structure of physical motion? To examine this, we propose Sensorimotor Alignment ($S^2$), a training-free offline metric that measures how well a model's sensory representation aligns with the geometry of physical motion. We find that $S^2$ correlates positively with downstream robot task success across embodied model families, making it a low-cost offline proxy for prioritizing models before closed-loop evaluation. $S^2$ can also identify promising vision-language model (VLM) backbones even before costly fine-tuning into vision-language-action models (VLAs). Beyond this correlation, $S^2$ offers representation-level explanations for phenomena observed in VLAs and world action models (WAMs). With $S^2$, we extend PRH to embodied models and make sensorimotor alignment empirically measurable, offering insight into why an embodied model succeeds beyond its closed-loop success rate.

articles.title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
articles.content: Video foundation models have advanced rapidly in understanding and generating visual sequences, while video world models seek to capture the underlying dynamics of the world they depict. Despite their different objectives, both concern the relationship between video observations and an evolving world. This survey adopts world modeling as a unifying lens for examining these developments. Viewing an observed video as a partial, lossy, and temporally ordered projection of a latent temporal world, we organize the literature around four complementary operations: reading infers world properties from observed video; writing synthesizes video from specified or learned world conditions; sharing integrates understanding and generation through common modeling mechanisms; and interacting predicts and updates world states under actions and evolving observations. This perspective distinguishes temporal coherence in observed or generated sequences from consistency in the underlying world state. Across tasks, representations, models, datasets, and benchmarks, we trace a shift in emphasis from clip-level recognition and perceptual fidelity toward persistent state, controllable evolution, physical and causal validity, and evaluation grounded in interaction and downstream decisions, and we distill the open challenges that follow.

articles.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
articles.content: Test-time scaling has emerged as a key inference strategy for reasoning models, where a model generates a large number of candidate solutions in the hope of finding at least one correct solution. Running all candidate solutions to completion can be computationally demanding, so recent work prunes the candidate pool after generating only a short prefix, committing further computation only to the surviving candidates. Existing pruning strategies divide broadly into two categories: Quality-based methods assign a score to each partial solution and discard those predicted to ultimately lead to an incorrect final solution, while diversity-based methods select partial solutions that follow different reasoning trajectories and are therefore likely to cover different final solutions. The tension between these two objectives is an instance of exploration versus exploitation, yet little to no prior work on pruning exposes this trade-off directly, let alone optimizes it. In this paper, we introduce a pruning procedure that addresses this trade-off directly by optimizing pass@$k$ over the selected solution pool. In particular, it chooses the pool to maximize the probability that at least one of its partial solutions, when continued to completion, yields a correct answer. Because this objective simultaneously rewards high-quality partial solutions and penalizes redundancy among them, quality and diversity are naturally balanced by the criterion itself rather than through separate ad-hoc design choices. On eight open-weight reasoning models, our method outperforms existing quality-based and diversity-based pruning strategies. The gains are particularly pronounced when the pruning procedure keeps a moderate number of partial solutions for continued generation, highlighting the value of directly balancing quality and diversity during pruning.

articles.title: Phase Transition from Random Features to Fully Trainable Networks
articles.content: Constructing accurate and computationally tractable approximation spaces is a fundamental task in scientific computing. Partially trainable neural networks bridge fixed random features and fully adaptive representations. This paper quantifies a phase transition pattern in approximation bounds and observes analogous behavior in training errors: a rapid but smooth initial improvement followed by diminishing returns, with a sharper transition under greater initialization mismatch. Under polynomial spectral decay with exponent $α>1$ and leverage compatibility, we establish a squared $L_2$ approximation rate $\mathcal{O}((κ_P\log(m/δ)/m)^α)$ for two-layer networks of width $m$ and trainable proportion $P$, where $κ_P=(P/κ_1^*+(1-P)/κ_0^*)^{-1}$. The bound holds uniformly over the unit ball of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) with probability at least $1-δ$. The constants $κ_0^*$ and $κ_1^*$ quantify the fixed and trainable groups' sampling mismatches relative to the target RKHS. For spherical biased-ReLU features in dimension $d$, we verify these assumptions with $α=(d+2)/(d-1)$ and $κ_0^*=4\sqrt{2}τ(d+1)/d$ for initialization scale $τ\ge1$, and $κ_1^*=1$ under ridge leverage sampling. For $d=5$ and $τ=10$, a trainable proportion of approximately $4.1\%$ captures $90\%$ of the reduction in the approximation bound from $P=0$ to $P=1$. A structured three-layer example illustrates how a few trainable first-layer neurons exploit fixed downstream blocks through nonlinear composition. Numerical experiments across diverse settings, including networks with up to 15 layers, exhibit similar phase transitions in training errors.

articles.title: Reliable AI-Assisted Decisions via Selective Auditing
articles.content: We consider online monitoring of an AI system that produces a sequence of decisions. At each round, the system outputs a proposed decision together with a confidence score estimating the trustworthiness of the decision. The decision and confidence score need not be produced by the same model: for example, one agent may propose a decision, while a separate verifier agent evaluates it and outputs a correctness or safety score. Based on this information, we must decide whether to accept the AI decision automatically or consult an expert, such as a human auditor, who reviews the proposal and either accepts or corrects it. We formulate this task as an online constrained optimization problem in which the goal is to minimize the frequency of expert auditing while guaranteeing that the fraction of AI errors that go unaudited stays below a user-defined threshold. We derive a family of algorithms with provable error-control guarantees with no assumptions, including a method that is optimally efficient: it asymptotically attains the best achievable auditing rate for both adversarial and i.i.d. data streams. Experiments on screening harmful requests to large language models, qualitative text annotation, and data labeling show that our methods achieve valid error control in practice while substantially reducing the need for human auditing compared to baselines.

articles.title: OpenTac: An Open Ecosystem for Customizable, Scalable, and Transferable 3D Tactile Sensing
articles.content: We present OpenTac, a novel sensor and a full-stack ecosystem for tactile skins that are highly customizable, scalable, and readily deployed in downstream robot control and learning applications. Our core contribution is twofold. First, we develop a scalable resistive tactile skin with a structured deformable overlay that converts tangential loading into spatially varying pressure. Differential responses across neighboring "taxels" support decoding of local shear vectors, and the common-mode response encodes normal force. Second, we provide a highly customizable sensor design tool that is able to automatically generate fabrication files for these tactile skins from 2D outlines and developable 3D surfaces, including from abstract descriptions such as text (e.g., "design a sensor for a size 9 shoe insole"). We develop an ecosystem around the OpenTac sensor, including the CAD design tool, a sensor simulator, cross-sensor transfer, and fast/adaptive data acquisition. We demonstrate the broad applicability of the OpenTac-CAD sensor design tool by designing and fabricating more than 30 sensors across a variety of robot embodiments. We characterize the three-dimensional tactile fields produced by OpenTac with a commercial, high-precision force/torque sensor. We demonstrate the broad applicability of 3D tactile sensing across contact-rich feedback control and manipulation policy learning on four real-world robot embodiments. Additionally, adaptive acquisition enables kilohertz-rate partial readouts, exceeding full-array raster scanning on the same sensor by 19.2X at 16 sampled taxels per update for a 1024-taxel skin. We provide all hardware, software, and result videos are at opentac.github.io

articles.title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
articles.content: Auditing whether a text-to-image (T2I) model was fine-tuned on a particular image collection is difficult: a model can absorb collection-level visual characteristics without reproducing training images. Proactive dataset-use auditing plants a shared signal in a dataset before release, then later checks whether that signal appears in a suspect model's generated outputs. Existing approaches often trade off verifiability, fidelity, robustness, and deployability. We introduce $\textbf{SpectralCanary}$, which uses a smooth low-pass mask to blend a fixed canary image into every collection image while leaving captions unchanged and requiring neither auxiliary generation nor per-image optimization. A lightweight verifier detects the transferred signal in suspect-model outputs. Across eight tests on the Pokemon dataset and three realistic data transformations, spanning two architectures families, SpectralCanary achieves the highest average per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR ($91.1\%$) and fixed threshold model-level accuracy using 30 generations ($94.8\%$) among the evaluated methods. Across five datasets spanning artistic, medical, satellite, and fashion domains with SD3.5, SpectralCanary averages $92.4\%$ per-generation TPR@$1\%$ FPR while preserving the released images (SSIM $0.989$, LPIPS $0.022$) with a near-zero mean change FID (mean $Δ$FID $0.05$) across datasets. Matched-energy ablations on Pokemon and ROCOv2 support our design choice, low-frequency placement transfers more reliably compared to mid/high-frequency placement. Under the evaluated adaptive attacks, the most effective removal requires aggressive modification and incurs more than $25$ $Δ$FID points. These results identify low-frequency visual signals as effective carriers for collection-level T2I audit traces.
